title: Uniform degree bounds for zeros of Abelian integrals
statement: For real polynomials \(H,P,Q\) of bounded degrees, bound the total isolated zeros, counted with multiplicity, of \(\int_{\gamma(t)}(P\,dx+Q\,dy)\) on the regular compact oval branches of \(H=t\), uniformly in the coefficients. Identically zero branches are excluded from the isolated-zero count.
status: As of November 2026, a finite explicit uniform bound is established by \citet[Theorem 2]{binyamininovikovyakovenko2010zeros} (preprint 2008; publication 2010). This addresses the precise first-period question, not Hilbert's full sixteenth problem. No exact earlier occurrence with this problem's quantifiers was found in the supplied index, which ends in 1982.

title: Local Langlands correspondence for GSp(4)
statement: For every characteristic-zero nonarchimedean local field \(F\), construct the finite \(L\)-packet classification of irreducible smooth \(GSp_4(F)\)-representations by admissible Weil--Deligne parameters in \(GSp_4(\mathbb C)\), with the specified natural compatibilities.
status: As of November 2026, solved in this scope by \citet[Main Theorem]{gantakeda2011local}, first circulated in 2007 and published in 2011. Vigneras's 1986 work is an important predecessor, not evidence that the complete exhaustion had already been proved in 1985.

title: Central section of a four-cube perpendicular to a main diagonal
status: As of November 2026: an elementary solved exercise. The section is a regular octahedron, proved in 1985-647.1 and independently checked by exact enumeration in this chapter. The index retains this explicit posed question while the E classification records that no research novelty is claimed.

title: Arithmetic occurrence and multiplicity in the automorphic spectrum
statement: For a fixed connected semisimple \(G/\mathbb Q\), determine which irreducible admissible restricted products of local representations occur in the discrete spectrum of \(L^2(G(\mathbb Q)\backslash G(\mathbb A))\), and their multiplicities; the unrestricted seminar question ranges over such groups. Distinguish this arithmetic classification from the already established decomposition by Eisenstein series.
status: As of November 2026: partly developed, with major classifications for specific families of groups, exemplified by Arthur's orthogonal/symplectic theory. The cited results do not give the unrestricted classification. The problem is too broad for a bounded new contribution without choosing a group and a particular packet or multiplicity. GP-1982-43 concerns a different automorphy question and is linked contextually, not merged.

title: Deciding identities in all finite-dimensional subspace lattices
statement: For a fixed field \(F\), is there an algorithm deciding whether two finite terms in sum and intersection have equal values on every tuple of subspaces in every finite-dimensional \(F\)-vector space? The concrete proposed reduction is to dimension \(1+\min\{\max(d(p),d(q)),\max(k(p),k(q))\}\), where \(d\) and \(k\) count joins and meets in the written terms.
status: Solved by the speaker: \citet[Lemma~1, Lemmas~2--3 and main theorem]{ryzhikova1987decidability}; received May 1986, Russian publication 1987, English translation 1988. As of November 2026, the exact identity-decision problem is settled; no complexity or general first-order decidability claim is added.

title: Index formulas for elliptic Fuchs-type operators with conic ends
statement: For a cone-elliptic regular singular differential operator on a compact manifold with isolated conic ends, and a specified closed \(L^2\) domain between its minimal and maximal domains, express its index by interior data, Mellin-symbol spectral data, and the chosen indicial-domain contribution. This is a reconstruction of the notebook's general ``index?'' question; its printed operator and domain are incomplete.
status: Developed by others. \citet[Prop.~1.3.16 and Cor.~2.4.7]{lesch1997fuchs} proves Fredholmness and an index formula in the constant-near-tip setting; Thm.~2.4.8 specializes it for first-order operators. Habilitation submitted 1993; preprint 1996; book 1997. As of November 2026 this is an established formulation, not a claim that every unqualified regular singular expression has a canonical index.

title: Reducibility and first singular vectors of Virasoro Verma modules
statement: For \(h,c\in\mathbb C\), determine when the Virasoro Verma module \(M(h,c)\) is reducible and determine its first positive grade containing a singular vector. The central-generator convention must be fixed before comparing formulas.
status: Solved before the present talk. \citet[\S3.2, Thm.~3.1 and corollary]{feiginfuchs1982invariant} gives the determinant factors and the first-grade criterion. Received September 1981, published 1982. As of November 2026, this recurrence remains E; the 1985 notebook's \(1/2\) coefficient must be corrected to \(1/16\).

title: Topology of real configuration realization spaces
statement: For a prescribed finite rank configuration or oriented-matroid type, determine the topology of its normalized real realization space; in particular, determine what homotopy types can occur. Incidence types and uniform chirotopes are distinguished. The exact modern universality theorem concerns stable equivalence to primary basic semialgebraic sets, with the uniform case restricted to open sets.
status: As of November 2026, general rank-three universality is established and was already announced before the talk by \citet[Theorem~3]{mnev1985varieties}. The modern formulation is \citet[Theorem~1]{adiprasitopadrol2017universality}. No claim of literal homeomorphism to every arbitrary algebraic variety is intended.

title: Isotopy within a fixed determinant-sign class
statement: For a uniform realizable rank-three oriented matroid on \(n\) labelled elements, is its normalized real realization space path connected? Equivalently, can matrices with the same nonzero maximal-minor signs be joined through the same sign class after fixing an oriented basis?
status: As of November 2026, the general answer is negative by universality, already available before this talk. The small-size assertion \(n\leq7\) is supported by a stronger known bound cited in \citet[introduction]{tsukamoto2013disconnected}. The exact uniform nineteen-element example attributed to Mn\"ev in the notebook remains an unresolved source identification; this does not make the general mathematical question open.

title: Universality in dimension four under simpliciality
statement: The notebook informally suggests ``more or less any topology'' for fixed-type simplicial four-polytope realization spaces. An editorial homotopy sharpening asks whether every nonempty finite simplicial-complex homotopy type occurs. The stronger precise modern conjecture asks whether every nonempty open primary basic semialgebraic set defined over \(\mathbb Z\) is stably equivalent to the homogenized realization space, modulo \(\mathrm{GL}_5(\mathbb R)\), of a neighborly (hence simplicial) four-polytope.
status: As of November 2026, no resolution of either fixed-four-dimensional universality formulation was found in the bounded search. General four-polytopes are universal by \citet[Main Theorem]{richtergebertziegler1995realization}; simplicial neighborly universality in \citet[Theorem~2]{adiprasitopadrol2017universality} allows growing dimension, and their Conjecture~4 retains dimension four and additionally requires neighborliness. The latest opened explicit open-status evidence is the 2024 compendium CG68--CG69; this is not an exhaustive proof of absence of a later result. The chapter establishes only contractibility for normalized history-compatible spaces of prescribed facet-stackings.

title: Recognizing Jacobians among principally polarized abelian varieties
statement: Characterize the period matrices of smooth compact connected complex curves among symmetric matrices with positive definite imaginary part, modulo the symplectic group. Require indecomposability in the KP formulation; distinguish this recognition problem from finding a chosen explicit ideal of the Jacobian locus.
status: As of November 2026: solved in the KP-recognition sense by Shiota, with earlier circulation documented separately, and refined by Krichever\textquotesingle s auxiliary linear equation. The exact unnamed relations in the seminar margin cannot be reconstructed. Earlier items 1974-336.5 and 1982-592.6 are contextual links, not asserted occurrences of this precise question.
